Sri Shailesh Kumar Shukla, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Abhinav Tripathi preferred
'vakalatnama' on behalf of opposite party no.2, which is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Narayan Singh Kushwaha, learned counsel for the appellants, Sri Shailesh Kumar Shukla, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Abhinav Tripathi, counsel for opposite party no. 2 and learned AGA for the State.
3.

Etah in Session Case No. 254 of 2024 (State vs. Vipin Kumar and Others) under Sections 147, 341,

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that factual matrix of the matter is related to a civil dispute, which is pertaining between the parties and the same is evident through narration of the FIR, wherein it has been mentioned that the suit for cancellation of sale deed preferred at the behest of opposite party no. 2 is still pending, whereas it is undisputed that the land, subject matter of the suit preferred at the behest of opposite party no. 2, has already been mutated against the name of appellant no. 2 and as such the learned counsel for the appellants submitted that when the opposite party no. 2 failed to obtain any favourable order from the competent court, he preferred the instant FIR by way of giving entire dispute with criminal color and all the appellants were dragged into unwarranted criminal litigation.

Regarding attraction of Sections 147, 341 and 420 IPC are concerned, the same is only on the basis of the narration of the FIR through which it has been tried to demonstrate that the sale deed performed by one of the co-accused i.e., Bipin, who is the step brother of opposite party no. 2 and as such the same is not attracted specifically against the appellants.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants also submitted that being the bonafide purchaser and witness over the registered sale deed, the appellants were unnecessary implicated while preferring FIR against the step brother of opposite party no. 2.
The entire allegation whatsoever has been put-forward is basically related to other co-accused, who is the step brother of opposite party no. 2.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer made in the appeal by way of rebutting the stand taken up by learned counsel for the appellants and submitted that once the civil suit preferred at the behest of opposite party no. 2 for cancellation of the sale deed and during pendency of the same, it is the appellants who illegally entered into the agricultural plots of the opposite party no. 2 and started carrying agricultural work and tried to take illegal possession of the same.

The aforesaid incident has been narrated by opposite party no. 2 which has been registered as Case Crime No. 133 of 2023 under Sections 147, 341, 420,
504, 506, 120-B IPC and under Section 3(2)V of SC/ST Act.
7.

After having the rival submissions extended by learned counsel for the parties and by bare perusal of the record appended alongwith the instant appeal, it is crystal clear that the relevant sections i.e.,
Sections 147, 341 and 420 IPC is not attracting the appellants in pursuance to the narration of the FIR, so far as regarding Section 3(2)V of SC/ST Act once the property does not belongs to the opposite party no. 2, the same cannot be fastened against the appellants.

Rather the role of the appellants were very limited for implicating them only on the basis of the endorsement of themselves being the witness over the registered sale deed executed by other co-accused who is the step brother of the opposite party no. 2.

The entire proceedings which culminated into order impugned the present appeal is complex matter of fact which can only be adjudicated and decided by the competent court of Civil Judge where the suit for cancellation of sale deed is still pending,

2 which is apparent from the FIR itself.

sentences.text: So far as the crime committed by the appellants which attracted Sections 147, 341, 420, 504, 506, 120-B IPC and under Section 3(2)V of SC/ST Act is not at all covering the appellants which is apparent from the records itself.
8. Without expressing any specific opinion, order dated 13.03.2024 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Etah is set-aside.

Matter is remanded back to the learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Etah for taking fresh view after considering the specific role assigned and demonstrated through the FIR as well as the chargesheet which contains several evidences and statement recorded during investigation and after considering the same at the stage of Section 190 Cr.P.C., the same has to be passed with due consideration of the grounds taken up in the instant appeal.
9. The appeal stands allowed accordingly.
